chosen_property.label: about
chosen_property.justification: The schema.org property 'about' matches the subject→object direction of Event→Thing and fits all observed signatures.

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: claimReviewed
candidates.comment: A summary relation for a claim review, providing a short text of the specific claims being reviewed. Also called "reviewed claim", "claim summary", "subject of review". Examples: "Fact-check review claimReviewed 'Eating apples cures cancer'", "Product claim review claimReviewed 'This product doubles battery life'".

candidates.label: appearance
candidates.comment: An appearance relation between a claim and a creative work where that claim is found or occurs. Also called occurrence in, mentioned in, found in. Examples: "A claim's appearance is in 'News Article X'.", "The factual claim's appearance is in 'Research Paper Y'."

candidates.label: description
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation between a thing and its textual description. Also called: item description, details, explanation. Examples: "Product" description "A versatile smartphone with advanced camera features.", "Event" description "An annual conference for tech enthusiasts.", "Person" description "A renowned scientist and author.". Distinct from disambiguatingDescription, which is specifically for disambiguation.

candidates.label: associatedClaimReview
candidates.comment: A claim review related to another review by common content, topic, or claim. Also called: related claim review, linked claim assessment. Examples: "Review 'MediaReview of Article' associatedClaimReview 'ClaimReview of Statement'", "Review 'FactCheck' associatedClaimReview 'Another FactCheck'". Distinct from associatedMediaReview, which links to a media review.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: claimInterpreter
candidates.comment: An interpretation relation between a claim and the organization or person who interpreted it from media content. Also called "interpreted by", "claim analyst", "fact-checker". Examples: "News claim claimInterpreter FactCheck.org", "Social media claim claimInterpreter Jane Doe".

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: firstAppearance
candidates.comment: A first appearance relation between a claim and the creative work where it was initially known to occur. Also called: initial publication, original mention, debut in. Examples: "Claim: Earth is flat" first appearance "Ancient Greek Texts", "Claim: COVID-19 is a hoax" first appearance "Social Media Post", "Claim: New drug cures cancer" first appearance "Unverified Online Article".

chosen_property.label: location
chosen_property.justification: The schema.org property 'location' matches the subject→object direction of Event→Place and covers all observed signatures.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: geographicArea
candidates.comment: A geographic area relation between an audience and the administrative area it is associated with. Also called: target region, audience location, demographic area. Examples: "Local News Audience" geographic area "Springfield County", "National Election Voters" geographic area "United States", "European Market Audience" geographic area "European Union".

candidates.label: deathPlace
candidates.comment: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

candidates.label: locationCreated
candidates.comment: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: spatial
candidates.comment: A general spatial relation between a creative work and a place, used when more specific location properties are not applicable. Also called "related to place", "takes place in", "associated location", "geographic context". Examples: "The novel has spatial Paris", "The painting's spatial is a rural landscape", "This document's spatial is the Amazon rainforest.". Distinct from spatialCoverage, which indicates the specific geographic focus of the content.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: geo
candidates.comment: A geo relation between a place and its geographical coordinates or shape. Also called: geographic location, coordinates, spatial data. Examples: "Eiffel Tower" geo "Latitude: 48.8584, Longitude: 2.2945", "Central Park" geo "Polygon GeoShape", "Mount Everest" geo "Point GeoCoordinates".

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: spatialCoverage
candidates.comment: A geographic focus relation between a creative work and the place(s) that are the primary subject or focus of its content. Also called "geographic scope", "covered area", "location focus", "content location". Examples: "A weather dataset has spatialCoverage New York State", "The historical map's spatialCoverage is ancient Rome", "This research paper's spatialCoverage is the Arctic region.". Distinct from spatial, which is a more general spatial association when the specific focus is not known.

candidates.label: hasMap
candidates.comment: A map relation between a place and its associated map or map URL. Also called map of, location map, geographical map. Examples: "A restaurant has a map of its location.", "The park has a map showing its trails.", "This place has a map URL."

chosen_property.label: issuedBy
chosen_property.definition: The organization that issued a weather-related warning or watch.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property fits 'HurricaneWatch→GovernmentOrganization' and 'FloodingWarning→GovernmentOrganization' in the as_is direction.

candidates.label: issuedBy
candidates.comment: An issuing authority relation between a certification, permit, or ticket and the organization that granted or provided it. Also called granted by, provided by, authorized by, issuer. Examples: A driver's license is issuedBy 'Department of Motor Vehicles'. A concert ticket is issuedBy 'Ticketmaster'. A professional certification is issuedBy 'Certification Body X'.

candidates.label: recordLabel
candidates.comment: A record label relation between a music release and the organization that issued it. Also called issued by, released by, label. Examples: "An album release is on the record label 'Universal Music Group'.", "A single release is on the record label 'Atlantic Records'.", "A compilation album is on the record label 'Sony Music'."

candidates.label: publishedBy
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a publication event and the organization or person responsible for it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book's publication event was published by 'Penguin Random House'.", "A journal article's publication event was published by 'Elsevier'.", "A blog post's publication event was published by 'Jane Doe'.". Distinct from publisher, which refers to the publisher of the creative work itself.

candidates.label: publisher
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a creative work or financial incentive and the organization or person that publishes it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book has a publisher 'Penguin Random House'.", "A research paper has a publisher 'Nature Publishing Group'.", "A financial incentive has a publisher 'Government Agency'.". Distinct from publishedBy, which refers to the agent of a specific publication event.

candidates.label: dateIssued
candidates.comment: A temporal issuance relation between a ticket and the date it was issued. Also called: issuance date, date of issue, ticket date. Examples: "Concert Ticket" date issued "2023-04-01", "Flight Ticket" date issued "2023-01-10T14:30:00Z", "Parking Permit" date issued "2023-07-01".

candidates.label: issuedThrough
candidates.comment: A service channel relation between a permit and the specific service used to obtain it. Also called obtained via, granted through, service channel. Examples: A building permit was issuedThrough 'Online Permit Application System'. A fishing license was issuedThrough 'State Wildlife Service'. A visa was issuedThrough 'Consular Services Department'. Distinct from issuedBy, which is the organization, not the service.

candidates.label: issueNumber
candidates.comment: A publication identifier relation between a publication issue and its specific identifying number or designation within a series. Also called issue ID, volume number, edition number, publication identifier. Examples: A journal issue has an issueNumber of '5'. A comic book has an issueNumber of 'Vol. 2, Issue #3'. A magazine has an issueNumber of 'Summer 2023'. Distinct from volumeNumber, which is for the larger volume a publication issue belongs to.

candidates.label: recognizedBy
candidates.comment: A recognition relation between a credential and the organization that acknowledges its validity or value. Also called accredited by, validated by, acknowledged by. Examples: "A university degree is recognized by 'the Ministry of Education'.", "A professional certification is recognized by 'an industry association'.", "A medical license is recognized by 'the Medical Board'."

candidates.label: manufacturer
candidates.comment: A manufacturing relation between a product and the organization that produced it. Also called: produced by, made by, fabricated by. Examples: "Smartphone manufacturer Apple", "Automobile manufacturer Toyota", "Furniture manufacturer IKEA".

candidates.label: byMonthDay
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the month on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "day of month", "monthly day recurrence", "on day of month". Examples: "Rent payment schedule byMonthDay 1", "Board meeting schedule byMonthDay 15".

chosen_property.label: relatedEvent
chosen_property.definition: A temporal or causal connection between two weather-related events.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property fits the subject→object direction of HurricaneWatch→TropicalStormFormation and FloodingWarning→TropicalStormFormation.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: deathDate
candidates.comment: A temporal event relation between a person and their date of death. Also called: date of demise, passing date, decease date. Examples: "Historical Figure" death date "1963-11-22", "Family Member" death date "2020-05-10". Distinct from birthDate, which is the date of birth.

candidates.label: departureTime
candidates.comment: A temporal event relation between a trip and its expected departure time. Also called: scheduled departure, leaving time, takeoff time. Examples: "Flight" departure time "2023-11-01T08:00:00Z", "Bus Trip" departure time "14:30:00", "Train Journey" departure time "2023-12-25T10:00:00". Distinct from arrivalTime, which is the expected arrival time.

candidates.label: temporal
candidates.comment: A general temporal relation between a creative work and a date or time, used when more specific temporal properties are not applicable. Also called "related to time", "time context", "associated temporal period", "timeframe". Examples: "The novel has temporal the 19th century", "The painting's temporal is the Renaissance era", "This document's temporal is the year 2020.". Distinct from temporalCoverage, which indicates the specific time period the content applies to.

candidates.label: datasetTimeInterval
candidates.comment: A temporal applicability relation between a dataset and its relevant time range. Also called: dataset time range, temporal coverage, data period. Examples: "Census Data" dataset time interval "2011", "Historical Weather Data" dataset time interval "1950-2000", "Economic Survey" dataset time interval "2022-01-01/2022-12-31".

candidates.label: data
candidates.comment: An association relation between an instantaneous event and the data linked to it. Also called: event data, associated data, event information. Examples: "Sensor Reading Event" data "temperature: 25C, humidity: 60%", "Log Entry Event" data "User 'admin' logged in from IP 192.168.1.1", "System Alert Event" data "Error code 500: Database connection failed".

candidates.label: eventStatus
candidates.comment: An event status relation between an event and its current status type. Also called "event condition", "status of event", "event state". Examples: "Event 'Concert' eventStatus 'EventCancelled'", "Event 'Meeting' eventStatus 'EventScheduled'", "Event 'Festival' eventStatus 'EventRescheduled'".

candidates.label: coverageStartTime
candidates.comment: A temporal boundary relation between a live blog posting and the time when its event coverage begins. Also called: coverage start, reporting start time, live blog commencement. Examples: "Election Night Live Blog" coverage start time "2024-11-05T18:00:00Z", "Sports Event Live Update" coverage start time "2023-07-15T14:00:00Z", "Conference Live Blog" coverage start time "2023-10-27T09:00:00Z". Distinct from coverageEndTime, which indicates when coverage concludes.

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: guidelineSubject
candidates.comment: A guideline subject relation between a medical guideline and the medical conditions, treatments, or other entities it addresses. Also called: guideline topic, subject matter, focus. Examples: "AHA Guideline for Hypertension" guideline subject "Hypertension", "NICE Guideline for Diabetes" guideline subject "Type 2 Diabetes", "WHO COVID-19 Guidelines" guideline subject "COVID-19". Distinct from guideline, which is the guideline itself.

candidates.label: mainEntity
candidates.comment: A main entity relation between a creative work and the primary entity it describes. Also called: primary subject, about entity, central topic. Examples: "Wikipedia Article mainEntity Albert Einstein", "News Report mainEntity The Election", "Research Paper mainEntity Quantum Physics". Distinct from mainEntityOfPage, which indicates the page for which this thing is the main entity.

candidates.label: studySubject
candidates.comment: An investigative relation between a medical study and the medical entity (condition, therapy, drug, etc.) that is being investigated. Also called "subject of investigation", "research focus", "entity studied", "trial subject". Examples: "The medical study has studySubject a new drug", "The clinical trial's studySubject is a specific medical condition", "This study investigates a studySubject therapy."

candidates.label: itemOffered
candidates.comment: A transaction subject relation between a demand or offer and the specific item, product, service, or event being requested or provided. Also called offered item, demanded item, subject of offer, product/service offered. Examples: An offer has an itemOffered of 'a new car'. A demand has an itemOffered of 'web design service'. An offer has an itemOffered of 'a concert ticket'. Distinct from itemReviewed, which is the subject of a review, not an offer/demand.

candidates.label: itemReviewed
candidates.comment: A review subject relation between an aggregate rating or review and the entity that is being evaluated or rated. Also called reviewed item, rated item, subject of review, evaluated entity. Examples: A review has an itemReviewed of 'Restaurant X'. An aggregate rating has an itemReviewed of 'Movie Y'. A product review has an itemReviewed of 'Smartphone Z'. Distinct from itemOffered, which is the subject of an offer or demand.

candidates.label: specialty
candidates.comment: A categorization of a webpage's content by its domain specialty. Also called "domain expertise", "content area", "subject specialty", "field of study". Examples: "This medical webpage has specialty Cardiology", "The research paper's specialty is Artificial Intelligence", "The blog post's specialty is Vegan Cooking."

candidates.label: aspect
candidates.comment: A specific area or topic of medical practice considered on a medical webpage. Also called: medical topic, health aspect, clinical focus. Examples: "MedicalWebPage 'Diabetes' aspect 'diagnosis'", "MedicalWebPage 'Flu' aspect 'treatment'", "MedicalWebPage 'Cancer' aspect 'prognosis'."

candidates.label: hasHealthAspect
candidates.comment: A health aspect relation between health topic content and the specific health aspect it addresses. Also called content aspect, topic aspect, health focus. Examples: "Health topic content has a health aspect of 'treatment'.", "The article has a health aspect of 'self-care'.", "This content addresses a health aspect of 'overview'."

chosen_property.label: startDate
chosen_property.justification: The schema.org property 'startDate' matches the subject→object direction of Event→Date and covers all observed signatures.

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. The cancelled concert had a previous start date of '2023-07-01T19:00:00'. The postponed meeting's previous start date was 'last Monday'. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: contentReferenceTime
candidates.comment: A temporal reference relation for a creative work, indicating the specific date and time described or emphasized within its content. Also called "event time", "depicted time", "time of content". Examples: "News article contentReferenceTime '2023-10-26T14:00:00Z'", "Historical documentary contentReferenceTime '1945-09-02'".

candidates.label: scheduledTime
candidates.comment: The specific date or date and time when an action is planned to occur. Also called planned time, scheduled date, appointment time. Examples: `Meeting Action` scheduledTime `2023-10-26T10:00:00`, `Delivery Action` scheduledTime `2023-11-01`, `Maintenance Action` scheduledTime `2023-12-05T14:30:00`.

candidates.label: startTime
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning time of an action, reservation, or media segment. Also called "beginning time", "commencement time", "start of action", "reservation time". Examples: "The reservation has startTime 7:00 PM", "The action's startTime was 10:30 AM", "The media clip's startTime is 00:01:15.". Distinct from startDate, which specifies a date, while startTime focuses on the time of day or an offset.

candidates.label: byMonthDay
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the month on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "day of month", "monthly day recurrence", "on day of month". Examples: "Rent payment schedule byMonthDay 1", "Board meeting schedule byMonthDay 15".

candidates.label: temporal
candidates.comment: A general temporal relation between a creative work and a date or time, used when more specific temporal properties are not applicable. Also called "related to time", "time context", "associated temporal period", "timeframe". Examples: "The novel has temporal the 19th century", "The painting's temporal is the Renaissance era", "This document's temporal is the year 2020.". Distinct from temporalCoverage, which indicates the specific time period the content applies to.

candidates.label: byMonth
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the month(s) of the year on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "months of year", "monthly recurrence", "in month". Examples: "Annual conference schedule byMonth 10", "Quarterly report schedule byMonth 3,6,9,12".

candidates.label: deathDate
candidates.comment: A temporal event relation between a person and their date of death. Also called: date of demise, passing date, decease date. Examples: "Historical Figure" death date "1963-11-22", "Family Member" death date "2020-05-10". Distinct from birthDate, which is the date of birth.

chosen_property.label: hasMaximumSustainedWindSpeed
chosen_property.definition: The maximum sustained wind speed associated with a tropical storm.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property fits the subject→object direction of TropicalStorm→WindSpeed.

candidates.label: maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity
candidates.comment: A physical attendee capacity relation between an event and the maximum number of individuals who can physically attend. Also called: in-person capacity, venue limit, on-site capacity. Examples: "Hybrid Conference maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity 500", "Live Concert maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity 10000", "Workshop maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity 30". Distinct from maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity, which refers to online attendees.

candidates.label: speed
candidates.comment: A quantitative value representing the speed range of a vehicle. Also called "vehicle speed", "maximum speed", "speed capability", "velocity range". Examples: "The car has speed 200 KMH", "The boat's speed is 30 knots", "This vehicle's speed range is 0-120 mph."

candidates.label: maximumAttendeeCapacity
candidates.comment: An attendee capacity relation between an event or place and the total number of individuals it can accommodate. Also called: maximum occupancy, total capacity, attendee limit. Examples: "Concert Venue maximumAttendeeCapacity 5000", "Conference Room maximumAttendeeCapacity 100", "Public Park maximumAttendeeCapacity 10000".

candidates.label: maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity
candidates.comment: A virtual attendee capacity relation between an event and the maximum number of individuals who can attend online. Also called: online capacity, virtual participant limit, streaming capacity. Examples: "Hybrid Conference maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity 2000", "Webinar maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity 500", "Online Class maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity 100". Distinct from maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity, which refers to in-person attendees.

candidates.label: maxValue
candidates.comment: An upper value relation between a monetary amount, property value, property value specification, or quantitative value and the highest value of a characteristic or property. Also called: maximum limit, upper bound, highest possible value. Examples: "Temperature Range maxValue 30", "Age Limit maxValue 65", "Credit Score maxValue 850". Distinct from maxPrice, which specifically refers to the highest price in a range.

candidates.label: maximumIntake
candidates.comment: A maximum intake relation between a dietary supplement, drug, drug strength, or substance and its recommended maximum dose schedule. Also called: maximum dosage, recommended limit, upper intake level. Examples: "Vitamin C Supplement maximumIntake '2000 mg per day'", "Pain Reliever maximumIntake '8 tablets in 24 hours'", "Caffeine maximumIntake '400 mg per day'".

candidates.label: roofLoad
candidates.comment: The maximum permissible weight that can be carried on the roof of a vehicle, including cargo and any installations. Also called roof capacity, maximum roof weight, roof rack load limit. Examples: `SUV Model X` roofLoad `75 kg`, `Sedan Model Y` roofLoad `50 kg`, `Van Model Z` roofLoad `100 kg`. Distinct from `cargoVolume`, which refers to the internal cargo space.

candidates.label: maximumEnrollment
candidates.comment: An enrollment capacity relation between an educational or occupational program and the maximum number of students who can be enrolled. Also called: enrollment limit, student capacity, maximum participants. Examples: "Master's Program maximumEnrollment 50", "Workshop maximumEnrollment 20", "Online Course maximumEnrollment 500".

candidates.label: suggestedMaxAge
candidates.comment: A numerical value indicating the maximum recommended age in years for an audience or user. Also called "maximum age", "upper age limit", "age cap". Examples: "The game has suggestedMaxAge 12", "The audience specification includes suggestedMaxAge 65", "This content is suitable up to suggestedMaxAge 18.". Distinct from suggestedAge, which specifies a range, and suggestedMinAge, which specifies only the minimum.

candidates.label: childMaxAge
candidates.comment: A demographic specification for a parent audience, indicating the maximal age of a child. Also called "maximum child age", "upper age limit for child", "child age cap". Examples: "Parent audience for toddlers childMaxAge 3", "Parent audience for teens childMaxAge 17". Distinct from childMinAge, which specifies the minimal age.

candidates.label: fromLocation
candidates.comment: A from location relation between an exercise, move, or transfer action and the original place of the object or agent before the action occurred. Also called: origin location, starting point, departure place. Examples: "Package Delivery" from location "Warehouse A", "Person Moving" from location "Old Apartment", "Data Transfer" from location "Server Room 1". Distinct from toLocation, which is the destination after the action.

candidates.label: toLocation
candidates.comment: A destination location relation between an action (like exercise, insert, move, or transfer) and the final place of the object or agent after the action. Also called destination, final location, arrival place. Examples: "MoveAction toLocation 'New York'", "TransferAction toLocation 'Warehouse B'", "ExerciseAction toLocation 'gym'". Distinct from location, which is the general place where something is or occurs.

candidates.label: muscleAction
candidates.comment: A description of the movement generated by a muscle. Also called muscle function, muscle movement, action of muscle. Examples: "Biceps Brachii muscleAction 'flexion of elbow'", "Triceps Brachii muscleAction 'extension of elbow'", "Deltoid muscleAction 'abduction of shoulder'".

candidates.label: functionalClass
candidates.comment: A functional class relation between a joint and the degree of mobility it permits. Also called: joint mobility, range of motion, movement classification. Examples: "Knee Joint" functional class "Diarthrosis (freely movable)", "Skull Sutures" functional class "Synarthrosis (immovable)", "Vertebral Joints" functional class "Amphiarthrosis (slightly movable)".

candidates.label: speed
candidates.comment: A quantitative value representing the speed range of a vehicle. Also called "vehicle speed", "maximum speed", "speed capability", "velocity range". Examples: "The car has speed 200 KMH", "The boat's speed is 30 knots", "This vehicle's speed range is 0-120 mph."

candidates.label: steeringPosition
candidates.comment: A specification of the steering wheel's position in a vehicle, typically for cars. Also called "steering wheel side", "driver's side", "left-hand drive", "right-hand drive". Examples: "The car has steeringPosition LeftHandDriving", "This vehicle's steeringPosition is RightHandDriving", "The steeringPosition indicates where the driver sits."

candidates.label: distance
candidates.comment: A distance relation between an exercise action or travel action and the length travelled. Also called "travelled distance", "route length", "journey distance". Examples: "Exercise action 'Running' distance '10 km'", "Travel action 'Road Trip' distance '500 miles'", "Cycling activity distance '25 mi'".

candidates.label: providerMobility
candidates.comment: A provider mobility relation between a service and its characteristic of being static or dynamic. Also called service mobility, mobility type. Examples: "A taxi service has a provider mobility 'dynamic'.", "A fixed-location restaurant service has a provider mobility 'static'.", "A mobile car wash service has a provider mobility 'dynamic'."

candidates.label: isRelatedTo
candidates.comment: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Examples: A smartphone isRelatedTo 'a smart watch'. A car service isRelatedTo 'car insurance'. A book isRelatedTo 'a movie adaptation'. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.

candidates.label: isLocatedInSubcellularLocation
candidates.comment: A subcellular localization relation between a biochemical entity and its specific location within a cell. Also called found in subcellular location, localized to, present in subcellular compartment. Examples: A protein is isLocatedInSubcellularLocation 'cytoplasm'. DNA is isLocatedInSubcellularLocation 'nucleus'. Mitochondrial enzymes are isLocatedInSubcellularLocation 'mitochondrion'.

chosen_property.label: couldReachStrength
chosen_property.definition: The potential strength that a tropical storm could reach.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property fits the subject→object direction of TropicalStorm→StormStrength.

candidates.label: serviceLocation
candidates.comment: The physical place where a service can be accessed or obtained. Also called service access point, physical service location, service venue. Examples: `Bank Service Channel` serviceLocation `Bank Branch`, `Government Service Channel` serviceLocation `City Hall`, `Repair Service Channel` serviceLocation `Repair Shop`. Distinct from `serviceArea`, which is the broader geographic region.

candidates.label: deathPlace
candidates.comment: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: geo
candidates.comment: A geo relation between a place and its geographical coordinates or shape. Also called: geographic location, coordinates, spatial data. Examples: "Eiffel Tower" geo "Latitude: 48.8584, Longitude: 2.2945", "Central Park" geo "Polygon GeoShape", "Mount Everest" geo "Point GeoCoordinates".

candidates.label: displayLocation
candidates.comment: A display location relation between a creative work or product and the place where it can be viewed or experienced in-person. Also called "viewing location", "exhibition place", "experience venue". Examples: "Painting 'Mona Lisa' displayLocation 'Louvre Museum'", "Product 'New Car Model' displayLocation 'Dealership Showroom'", "Sculpture displayLocation 'Art Gallery'".

candidates.label: foundingLocation
candidates.comment: A founding location relation between an organization and the place where it was established. Also called: place of origin, establishment location, birthplace. Examples: "Microsoft" founding location "Albuquerque, New Mexico", "Apple Inc." founding location "Los Altos, California", "Google" founding location "Menlo Park, California".

candidates.label: homeLocation
candidates.comment: A home location relation between a person and their residential contact point or place. Also called residence, dwelling, home address. Examples: "A person has a home location in London.", "Her home location is a specific address.", "The individual's home location is a contact point."

candidates.label: possibleComplication
candidates.comment: A medical attribute describing a potential unexpected and unfavorable evolution or outcome of a medical condition. Also called potential adverse event, risk, secondary condition, complication risk. Examples: Diabetes has a possible complication of 'kidney failure'. Surgery has a possible complication of 'infection'. A medical condition has a possible complication of 'worsening symptoms'.

candidates.label: containedInPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedInPlace 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedInPlace 'Paris'". Distinct from containedIn, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: potentialAction
candidates.comment: A behavioral attribute indicating an idealized action in which a thing could potentially serve as the object. Also called possible action, available action, actionable item. Examples: A product has a potential action 'BuyAction'. A book has a potential action 'ReadAction'. A movie has a potential action 'WatchAction'.

chosen_property.label: containedInPlace
chosen_property.justification: The schema.org property 'containedInPlace' matches the subject→object direction of TropicalStorm→Place (LakeBodyOfWater).

candidates.label: isRelatedTo
candidates.comment: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Examples: A smartphone isRelatedTo 'a smart watch'. A car service isRelatedTo 'car insurance'. A book isRelatedTo 'a movie adaptation'. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.

candidates.label: isrcCode
candidates.comment: A music recording identification relation between a music recording and its International Standard Recording Code. Also called ISRC identifier, recording code, music track ID. Examples: A music recording has an isrcCode of 'US-S1Z-99-00001'. A song has an isrcCode of 'GB-LFB-04-00001'. An album track has an isrcCode of 'QZ-F89-12-00001'. Distinct from iswcCode, which is for musical compositions, not recordings.

candidates.label: isicV4
candidates.comment: An industry classification relation between an organization, person, or place and its International Standard Industrial Classification of All Economic Activities (ISIC) Revision 4 code. Also called ISIC code, industry classification code, economic activity code. Examples: An organization has an isicV4 of '6201' (Computer programming activities). A person has an isicV4 of '8620' (Medical and dental practice activities). A place has an isicV4 of '5510' (Hotels and similar accommodation).

candidates.label: isResizable
candidates.comment: A model property relation indicating whether a 3D model can be scaled or resized. Also called resizable, scalable, adjustable size. Examples: A 3D model of a chair has isResizable set to 'true'. A 3D model of a building has isResizable set to 'false'. A 3D model of a character has isResizable set to 'true'.

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: member
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: belongs to, is a part of, participant in. Examples: "Club Organization member John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership member Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization member Partner Company". Distinct from memberOf, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: iswcCode
candidates.comment: A music composition identification relation between a music composition and its International Standard Musical Work Code. Also called ISWC identifier, composition code, musical work ID. Examples: A music composition has an iswcCode of 'T-034.045.001-6'. A song has an iswcCode of 'T-901.234.567-8'. A classical piece has an iswcCode of 'T-123.456.789-0'. Distinct from isrcCode, which is for music recordings, not compositions.

candidates.label: isVariantOf
candidates.comment: A product variation relation between a product or product model and the base product or product group from which it is a specific variant. Also called variant of, version of, derived from product, specific model of. Examples: A 'red iPhone 15' isVariantOf 'iPhone 15 Pro'. A 'size L t-shirt' isVariantOf 'Basic T-Shirt ProductGroup'. A 'diesel car model' isVariantOf 'Car Model X'. Distinct from isRelatedTo or isSimilarTo, as it implies a direct hierarchical relationship of variation from a base product or group.

candidates.label: memberOf
candidates.comment: A membership relation between an organization or person and the organization or program membership they belong to. Also called: belongs to, is a member of, affiliated with. Examples: "John Doe memberOf 'Local Sports Club'", "Acme Corp memberOf 'Industry Association'", "Jane Smith memberOf 'Premium Membership Tier'". Distinct from member, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: isGift
candidates.comment: A transaction intent relation indicating whether an order was placed as a gift for a recipient other than the buyer. Also called gift purchase, purchased as gift, gift order. Examples: An order has isGift set to 'true'. A purchase has isGift set to 'false'. A book order has isGift set to 'true' with gift wrapping.
